To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transcriptional regulation and expression pattern of the Bvgi phase virulence factor bipA is controlled by the relative affinities and spacing of multiple Bvg‐binding sites in the promoter region of the gene.
the bipA gene is transcribed in the Bvgi phase and that this regulation is mediated by BvgA.

bipA is a Bvg‐regulated virulence gene that is expressed in a Bvgi phase, that the bipA transcriptional regulatory region includes numerous BvgA‐binding sites, that BvgA binding is phase‐dependent and that the bipA promoter is a BvgAS‐regulated promoter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptional control of bipA
the regulation of virulence gene expression in Bordetella species
the regulation of virulence factor production in Bordetella species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BvgA regulon consists of at least four distinct groups of genes: (i) Bvg‐activated genes, (ii) Bvg‐reduced genes, (iii) Bvgi phase‐specific genes and (iv) Bvg‐independent genes.
the BvgA‐BvgS signal transduction system is a paradigm for how bacteria regulate the transcriptional expression of virulence factors.
BvgA is a global regulator that controls the expression of a wide variety of phenotypes and genes, including those that are unique to the Bvgi phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptional regulation for bipA is a model for the Bvgi phase of the BvgAS signal‐transduction system.
BvgA is a global regulator that controls the expression of a diverse set of virulence genes by a variety of regulatory mechanisms.
the Bvg regulon is not only a complex system of transcriptional regulation, but also a complex system of phase‐specific transcriptional control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BvgAS system can be used to modulate gene expression in an extremely flexible manner, which is likely to be important to the pathogenicity of these bacteria.

the BvgA regulon includes a diversity of genes that are regulated by multiple mechanisms, including phase‐dependent and ‐independent transcriptional control, post‐transcriptional regulation and phase‐specific protein–protein interactions.

transcription of bipA is controlled by the BvgAS signal‐transduction pathway, but that this pathway is capable of controlling a diversity of phenotypes, including a Bvgi phase that has not been previously recognized in Bordetella.
